---
title: "One-file Mathematical Learning Lab"
description: "Run the same invented delivery-data example across all mathematical and ML chapters."
---

## One dataset, multiple models

This lab deliberately keeps the **six original orders** constant while the mathematical questions change. Distance and item count form a matrix; fulfilment time is used as a regression label, a one-dimensional mixture observation, or a late/on-time classification label. PCA uses the two input features without looking at their times.

The code is **independently authored** and requires only Python 3.11+ with the standard library. It does not reproduce the uploaded textbook's code or exercises.

## Run it

~~~bash
python3 ai-mathematics/examples/delivery_ml_lab.py all
~~~

Run just one experiment:

~~~bash
python3 ai-mathematics/examples/delivery_ml_lab.py linear
python3 ai-mathematics/examples/delivery_ml_lab.py geometry
python3 ai-mathematics/examples/delivery_ml_lab.py calculus
python3 ai-mathematics/examples/delivery_ml_lab.py probability
python3 ai-mathematics/examples/delivery_ml_lab.py optimisation
python3 ai-mathematics/examples/delivery_ml_lab.py regression
python3 ai-mathematics/examples/delivery_ml_lab.py pca
python3 ai-mathematics/examples/delivery_ml_lab.py gmm
python3 ai-mathematics/examples/delivery_ml_lab.py svm
~~~

[Download the original Python source](delivery_ml_lab.py) or [view the source in GitHub](https://github.com/richardgong1987/knowledge-library/blob/main/ai-mathematics/examples/delivery_ml_lab.py).

## Test the mathematics

~~~bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s ai-mathematics/examples -p 'test_*.py'
~~~

Tests cover Gaussian elimination, consistency of gradient descent with the analytic regression solution, PCA unit-vector invariants, GMM mixture parameters and the SVM geometric-margin calculation.

## What the code does not claim

The SVM mode **demonstrates a valid separating hyperplane but does not train an SVM optimiser**. The GMM uses one-dimensional Gaussian components with variance safeguards, which is suitable for teaching EM but not arbitrary production data. Least squares uses normal equations for transparency; production software should use more stable methods when needed.
